cost.csv tail scanned for the shard spend counter.

0 makes this lane call no model at all. bin/lib/llm-gate.sh refuses BEFORE the vendor call and writes a zero-cost row_source=refused row, so the stop is visible in the ledger rather than being a lane that went quiet.

Comma/space list of the ONLY ladder rungs this lane may reach. Empty is every rung, i.e. today's ladder unchanged. A rung outside the list is refused before the call, so a cliff or a failure on the standing lane cannot descend into one that costs ~100x (#1141, the $793 descent).

Dollars this lane may spend in the current UTC day, summed from D1 cost_rows through GET /api/metrics/llm-spend — never from the box's own logs/cost.csv. A second, project-scoped ceiling is the lane.<id>.<project>.llm_usd_cap_day row, which is read only when somebody wrote it.
Read by bin/run-triage.sh as ${GROK_EFFORT:-}. Registered by BH-1165 so it is visible and settable; no reviewed min/max yet, so nothing is clamped.

Read by bin/run-triage.sh as ${RUNNER_TRIAGE:-claude}. Registered by BH-1165 so it is visible and settable: it NAMES a runner out of the closed list bin/agent-call.sh dispatches (claude|codex|openrouter|fireworks|grok|gemini, runner_ready refuses anything else), so it selects a lane rather than running a command — and which runner triage uses is the spend lever the $793 night turned on; no reviewed min/max yet, so nothing is clamped.
Read by bin/run-triage.sh as ${SCOPED_GROK_EFFORT:-medium}. Registered by BH-1165 so it is visible and settable; no reviewed min/max yet, so nothing is clamped.

Empty by default since BH-1510.2: the model is a database row, model_routes role 'triage.light', read through bin/lib/triage-shards-lib.sh:triage_model. Set this only to override that row on this box/lane; no reviewed min/max, nothing is clamped.
GitHub App token life a triage tick asks for before it arms; a shorter cached token is re-minted.

P2 cadence: minimum seconds between PAID triage ticks for this project (set per project: lane.run-triage.<project>.triage_min_interval_s). Capped at 86400: the daily sweep is the backstop. forced, daily-sweep, no-gate-state and event-wake are exempt. 0 is today (every gate RUN is bought).
P2 ceiling: paid triage ticks (counted at launch) per project per rolling 24h. forced, daily-sweep, no-gate-state and event-wake are exempt. 0 is no ceiling.

P2: hold the paid triage ticks that need the board (board-changed, daily-sweep, event-wake, no-gate-state, gate-fetch-failed) while the project cannot produce a build: no repo/board in fleet.conf, board fetch failing, or a state/triage-health/<project>.down marker. Queue, results and forced ticks proceed. One warn-digest line per project per day. 0 turns the check off.
P2: consecutive gate-fetch-failed ticks before the board counts as down (one re-probe first). 0 turns the fetch probe off.
P2: 1 makes a project with no repo checkout on its triage box unhealthy. Ships 0: bin/run-triage.sh runs without a checkout by design, so opt in per project once the checkout is confirmed.

BH-2526: build dirs bin/commented-mirror.sh turns into a job_artifacts commented row (or withdraws) per triage tick, oldest first; the rest are counted deferred and drained on later ticks. Not a whole number: the mirror logs one line and does nothing.
